mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in FEDFUNDS above 2% over two consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in GDPC1 exceeding 2% indicates a significant contraction in aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and depresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in UNRATE above 4% for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which raises wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in INDPRO below 97 for three consecutive months indicates weakening industrial production, reflecting supply-side contraction that reduces corporate earnings and drags equity prices lower over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly decline in both GDPC1 and HOUST by more than 1% signals a broad-based drop in economic activity and housing demand, which negatively impacts consumer spending and corporate revenues, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both decline by >1% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 50% of co-triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp monthly increase in FEDFUNDS of more than 0.75 percentage points, combined with a concurrent rise in CPIAUCSL above 3%, signals aggressive monetary tightening amid inflation, which increases risk-free rates and erodes equity valuations over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS change > 0.75% AND CPIAUCSL > 3% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 40% of co-triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in PAYEMS above 0.5% for four consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in RSAFS below 500,000 for six consecutive months signals a significant drop in consumer savings, which may indicate either sharply reduced precautionary balances or increased spending, but in the context of weak GDP growth, it forecasts negative equity returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.8%) in at least 50% of triggered episodes.
